document_title: Houston's 19,950 acres, and the answer owed October 26th
post_copy:
Commissioner Crowther, your department would keep a take-back clause on 885 acres at Port MacKenzie and waive it on 19,950 acres at Houston.

Senate Resources voted to subpoena you. You're due October 26th at 10 a.m.

What does the state get? Nothing for the land itself. AIDEA would pay survey and closing costs.

What is it for? Your department's decision says its scope does not include AIDEA's post-patent use.

Can the state take it back? At Port MacKenzie, if AIDEA doesn't use it within five years. At Houston, not if the waiver stands. The written reason is that a reverter would limit AIDEA's bonding.

First comes DNR's refusal to attend and the subpoena, then the land and its price, the committee's size test, both reverters and the dated record.

Is easier bonding for AIDEA worth giving up the state's take-back on about 31 square miles?

#AIDEA #MatSuBorough #AlaskaPublicLands

slides.kicker: UPDATE · ALASKA DNR TO THE SENATE, SEPTEMBER 22ND
slides.headline: "The Governor's office has not given us permission to attend."
slides.body: DECLINING AN OCTOBER 8TH HEARING ON 19,950 ACRES

slides.headline: Senators voted to subpoena him.
slides.body: On October 14th Senate Resources voted to subpoena Natural Resources Commissioner John Crowther. DNR confirmed a day later that he will appear on October 26th at 10 a.m.

slides.kicker2: What will he be asked to explain?
slides.headline: About 19,950 acres of state land, at no cost for the land.
slides.body: About 31 square miles, two miles north of Houston, to the Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority under the public and charitable use statute. AIDEA would cover survey and closing costs, not the land's value.

slides.kicker2: Is this what the statute is for?
slides.headline: 94 percent of other transfers under it were under 100 acres.
slides.body: This one is about 200 times that. The law sets no size limit, the Legislature's lawyer wrote, and he was not aware of any earlier transfer to AIDEA under it.

slides.kicker2: What will AIDEA do with it?
slides.headline: "The scope of this decision does not include AIDEA's post-patent use."
slides.body: The decision lists scalable data centers among AIDEA's possible uses. On October 8th AIDEA's director called a data center there implausible, Alaska's News Source reported.
labels: AIDEA'S USE AFTER PATENT NOT IN THIS DECISION'S SCOPE

slides.kicker2: What keeps it public after the deed?
slides.headline: Port MacKenzie's draft keeps a reverter. Houston's would waive it.
slides.body: DNR's Port MacKenzie decision includes a five year take-back clause on 885 acres. Without one, the Legislature's lawyer wrote on September 4th, no legal mechanism after patent keeps the land serving a public purpose.
labels: HOUSTON · 19,950 ACRES · REVERTER WOULD BE WAIVED
PORT MACKENZIE · 885 ACRES FIVE YEAR REVERTER INCLUDED

slides.headline: 41.8 miles of trail already cross it.
slides.body: They tie into the Haessler-Norris. The committee lists mushing, four-wheeling and snowmachining.

slides.headline: July 10th to October 26th
labels: DNR declines, citing the governor's office.

slides.headline: Why waive the reverter at Houston and keep it at Port MacKenzie?
slides.body: What should the first question be?

editor_notes_for_email: No.88 is an UPDATE of No.68 and No.85 on the Houston land conveyance to AIDEA, because the story moved this week. On September 22nd DNR declined the October 8th hearing in writing, saying the governor's office had not given it permission to attend. On October 14th Senate Resources voted to subpoena Commissioner Crowther, and DNR confirmed he will appear October 26th at 10 a.m. The new turn is DNR's own Port MacKenzie decision, which keeps a five year reverter on 885 acres while the Houston decision would waive it on 19,950. The honesty guards held on every frame. No data center is proposed at Houston. Data centers appear only as a use DNR's decision lists, and AIDEA's director called one implausible as Alaska's News Source reported. The reverter is always 'would be' waived because the Houston decision is preliminary. The 94 percent is the committee's figure from its October 8th overview and is attributed on slide 4. The parcel outline is traced after DNR's vicinity map, 19,733 traced acres against the 19,950 DNR states, and slides 3 and 6 say so. The hearing room on slides 1 and 9 is an illustration, not the Denali Room, and both are labelled ILLUSTRATION, as is the snow scene on slide 7. The Port MacKenzie decision is also preliminary (comments close October 21st), so the caption and slide 6 say it would keep or includes a reverter, never that it kept one. The vote count is left out because ADN and KTUU disagree about the sixth senator.
